hypothesis: The APK86 release's official GitHub run/release/source and transport multipart metadata should agree exactly and remain fail-closed under missing/extra files, renumbered chunks, stale size declarations, or source identity mismatch; syntax-only hashes cannot prove actual downloaded bytes.
input_hashes: Raft GitHub Release tag android-early-test-41812889049-1, release id433995856, API official 12 assets
Release body exact 3 logical file size/SHA256 declarations + signed target source field, with no actual binary downloaded
budget: One small source-only GitHub Actions CPU workflow, ubuntu24.04, six-minute limit; no ZIP2, Unity/LFS/binary download and no native request.
negative_controls: Missing/extra/duplicate auxiliary or transport asset refused
Malformed asset SHA declaration or body-vs-API APK digest mismatch refused
OBB and XAPK actual aggregate uploaded part sizes must equal declared logical byte counts
Multipart indices must be contiguous, unique, and bounded to 1GiB per part
Both whole and multipart same file rejected
A valid-looking malicious multipart SHA is NOT verifiable with metadata alone; content cryptographic verification flags always false
Even an actual successful native workflow plus matching release assets does not prove Android APK signature, OBB mount, XAPK reassembly or phone gameplay

limitations: This audit binds all submitted metadata to the same source/run, but a forged syntactically valid multipart digest remains indistinguishable without downloading part bytes against an independently trusted manifest.
